title: Breakpoint weekly KPI scratch
content:
Quick scratchpad for weekly KPI & micro-OKR check-in (Breakpoint method)
Owner: Arjun Nanda
Week window: 2024-10-14 -> 2024-10-27

Anchor objective: Improve hosted p50 inference latency for small chat model by ~8% while keeping cost change < +2%

Micro-KPIs (daily sampling):
- p50 latency (ms): baseline 122 -> target 112
- p95 latency (ms): baseline 320 -> soft target 290
- tokens/sec per GPU: baseline 48 -> target 55
- cost per 1k tokens: baseline $0.021 -> target <= $0.022

Breakpoint method (how I think about the week):
1) Anchor: the single smallest metric that must move (p50).
2) Signal: short-running experiments that can produce measurable deltas within 48h.
3) Friction: immediate blockers (infra/KMS, charts, rollout config) that will kill an experiment.
4) Capacity: time boxed tasks I can do solo vs things that need a collaborator.

Hypotheses:
1) Reducing batching window from 30ms -> 18ms for low-concurrency bursts will lower p50 by ~6-10% with <1.5% cost uplift.
2) Enabling prefix-KV cache for session reuse will increase tokens/sec by 8-12% for chat flows with reuse >60%.
3) Prompt rewrite to move long auxiliary context out of per-message tokens will lower p50 and cost for common queries.

Experiment ledger (quick):
- E1: Shorter batching window A/B on route /chat/small-model. Start: 2024-10-15. Owner: me. Metric: p50 delta, cost delta. Notes: canary at 5% traffic, synthetic traffic run at 80% live to verify tail. Status: running.
- E2: KV cache TTL adjust 2s->8s for demo cohort. Start: 2024-10-16. Owner: me. Metric: tokens/sec. Status: blocked by KMS policy; ticket JIRA-ENG-459.
- E3: Kernel schedule tweak (minor kernel selection) under canary. Planned start: 2024-10-20. Owner: Maya Cox. Metric: tokens/sec, p95. Status: planned.

Quick wins / low-friction fixes:
- Add ephemeral per-request trace flag to capture per-token latency slices (owner: Ellen Park). Ticket ref: CONFLUENCE-12345.
- Prompt rewrite: reduce context length for top-10 queries by moving non-critical content to system prompt. Owner: me.

Risks and failure modes:
- Increased burstiness -> p95 regressions. Mitigation: fallback to dedicated pool for high-latency, and automatic rollback.
- Delayed cost telemetry (12-18h) masks short regressions. Mitigation: add 1h sampled cost telemetry and alert on >5% uplift.
- KV cache changes might increase memory pressure on shared instances; watch OOM and evictions.

Notes to self:
- Keep any experiment <= 2 changes at once; prefer sequential toggles so signal attribution is clearer.
- Always add runbook snippet to the canary PR: how to rollback, who to ping, and a runbook check that sampling is present.
- Capture PR links and canary urls in this doc before merging.

Next steps (this sprint):
1) Finalize E1 canary config and deploy canary (target date 2024-10-18). Add alert p50 > baseline+5% -> auto rollback.
2) Unblock KMS conversation with infra to resume E2 (owner: me).
3) Run synthetic 1-hour load to validate tokens/sec uplift for E1.
4) Draft one-pager (1 page) with results and share in Friday async demo channel.

Reflection prompts for end-of-week retro:
- Which micro-KPI moved the needle most and why?
- Which experiment had an untested assumption that failed?
- What is the smallest automation that would have removed manual overhead?

Scratch pad (quick numbers copy-paste):
baseline_p50: 122
baseline_p95: 320
baseline_tokens_sec: 48
baseline_cost_1k: 0.021

Open questions:
- If p95 regresses slightly but p50 improves materially, what's the acceptable tradeoff for product? (ask PM)
- How to capture user-level reuse rate to better target KV cache TTL? (instrumentation ask)

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc: one place to copy metrics into PRs and async updates.
